name: Western foods made Japanese

axes.label: Where it is made or served

lineages.name: Napolitan, pasta and pizza
lineages.nameJa: ナポリタン・パスタ・ピザ

origin.place: Nagasaki (pasta); Yokohama (Napolitan, by one hotel’s account); Ebisu, Tokyo (delivery pizza)
origin.era: pasta from about 1883; Napolitan after 1952; delivery pizza 1985 (company claim)

cells.arrived: A missionary’s macaroni works; American soldiers’ spaghetti with ketchup during the occupation; an American delivery chain
cells.changed: Early domestic pasta blended several flours for Japanese taste; delivery pizza added tuna, teriyaki chicken and mayonnaise-potato toppings
cells.where: Hotel New Grand’s café in Yokohama for the hotel’s Napolitan; delivery chains for pizza
cells.marker: 1955 called the first year of pasta; durum-only domestic pasta in homes from about 1986

origin.place: Sasebo, Nagasaki (city tourism account); Ginza, Tokyo (McDonald’s Japan)

cells.arrived: Recipes from the US naval base in Sasebo; an American chain’s Japanese company
cells.changed: Teriyaki burgers (MOS 1973, McDonald’s Japan 1989), rice burgers, katsu burgers, a moon-viewing egg burger
cells.marker: Sasebo’s tourism site sets conditions for the name, including a head office in Sasebo

origin.place: Akasaka, Tokyo (first milk shop in the city); Hokkaido (most raw milk today)

cells.arrived: A Meiji government campaign for meat and milk
cells.changed: Milk in school lunches; strict naming rules for what may be called milk; a 1-litre carton built on an American base
cells.where: Hokkaido makes most raw milk, mostly for butter, cheese and other products; other regions mostly for drinking
cells.marker: Hokkaido 58% of national raw milk; domestic share of cheese eaten 15.5% (FY2025)
